renderer_issues.description: All three rendered pages report zero parse errors. Ten function-name substitutions occur in the Pr records. Proposed Release, ChargeRelease, and AirNStartTurn names add semantics not established by these initializer references; they remain unvalidated hypotheses rather than accepted corrections.

evidence.why: Canonical references are PrSpecialN1 callbacks, rendered with Release names.
Canonical PrSpecialAirN and PrSpecialN callback references are partially renamed in the reading view; the table alone cannot establish those proposed meanings.
Direct source-level access path and output types do not establish color, outline, or Game & Watch use.

renderer_issues.issue: The rendered GetGameWatchItemColor/GetGameWatchItemOutline names assert semantics not established by the accessor bodies. Canonical code instead reads hats[FTKIND_PICHU]->hat_dynamics[4], returning ftDynamicBones and x4 respectively.

evidence.why: The fallback is explicit and must be preserved in any semantic description.

renderer_issues.issue: The rendered GetHatJObj name omits the non-null-hat failure path, which returns the GObj cast to HSD_JObj rather than NULL.

renderer_issues: All three assigned rendered pages report zero parse errors and preserve canonical line alignment; no mechanical rendering defect was observed.

renderer_issues.description: All three pages report zero parse errors and preserve declaration lines. Some names remain canonical with a shadowed_binding status: ftKb_Init_UnkMotionStates6, ftKb_SpecialN_800F1420 and ftKb_SpecialN_800F5898 have proposed names in the footer but not in the reading view. This is an observed substitution limitation, not evidence that the proposed names are correct.

The view introduces behavioral and family changes not verifiable from these declarations, including SpecialHi-to-SpecialLw substitutions at lines 121–125 and SpecialNLg-to-Mr substitutions at lines 332–333. They remain hypotheses rather than accepted corrections.

The renderer reports zero parse errors and five substitutions. CheckSpecialNHold, SetNULL, ItemPKFlushSetNULL, and the two Enter names add behavioral hypotheses that cannot be verified from these prototypes. No structural rendering discrepancy was observed.

All three pages report zero parse errors and preserve declaration lines and signatures. The renderer reports shadowed_binding for ftKb_Init_GetMotionFileString at line 30 and ftKb_SpecialN_800F5898 at line 203; the latter has a proposed GetStarJObj name in the footer but remains canonical in the reading view. This is an explicit substitution limitation, not evidence that the proposed name is correct.

Function-name-only substitution can produce apparently inconsistent interfaces: for example, rendered GetMaxFuel/GetMaxFlameScale at lines 376–377 and GetIndex at line 404 retain canonical void return types. This review does not resolve whether those declarations or proposed names match current implementations.
